sentences.zh: 孟簡

translations.literal: Meng Jian
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jian

sentences.zh: 孟簡，字幾道，平昌人。

translations.literal: Meng Jian, style name Jidao, was a native of Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jian, whose style name was Jidao, was from Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 天後時同州刺史詵之孫。

translations.literal: He was the grandson of Shen, who had been prefect of Tong Prefecture in the time of Empress Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He was the grandson of Shen, prefect of Tongzhou during the reign of Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 工詩有名。

translations.literal: Skilled in poetry, he had a reputation for it.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in poetry and enjoyed a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，登宏辭科，累官至倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi examination, passed the Hongci examination, and rose through the ranks to become Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and the Hongci examination, and rose through the ranks to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎王叔文竊政，簡為子司，多不附之；

translations.literal: When Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Shuwen seized power, Jian served as his subordinate registrar but often did not side with him;
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Shuwen seized power, Jian served as his subordinate registrar but often refused to support him;

sentences.zh: 叔文惡之雖甚，亦不至擯斥。

translations.literal: though Shuwen hated him greatly, he still did not go so far as to drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: though Shuwen deeply resented him, he never went so far as to drive him from office.

sentences.zh: 尋遷司封郎中。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 元和四年，超拜諫議大夫，知匭事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe, he was promoted out of turn to Remonstrance Grandee and put in charge of the petition boxes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhe (809), he was promoted out of turn to remonstrance grandee and placed in charge of the petition boxes.

sentences.zh: 簡明於內典。

translations.literal: Jian was well versed in Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was well versed in Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔與給事中劉伯芻、工部侍郎歸登、右補闕蕭俛等，同就醴泉佛寺翻譯《大乘本生心地觀經》，簡最擅其理。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered him, together with Supervising Secretary Liu Boxu, Vice Minister of Works Gui Deng, and Right Remonstrance Supplementer Xiao Mian, to translate the Mahayana Sutra of the Mind-Ground of the Original Cause at Liquan Buddhist Temple; Jian was most adept at its principles.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (811), an edict ordered him, together with supervising secretary Liu Boxu, vice minister of works Gui Deng, and right remonstrance supplementer Xiao Mian, to translate the Mahayana Sutra of the Mind-Ground of the Original Cause at Liquan Buddhist Temple; Jian proved most adept at its doctrines.

sentences.zh: 王承宗叛，詔以吐突承璀為招討使。

translations.literal: When Wang Chengzong rebelled, an edict appointed Tuhu Chenghui as campaign commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong rebelled, an edict appointed Tuhu Chenghui campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 簡抗疏論之，坐語訐，出為常州刺史。

translations.literal: Jian submitted a memorial in protest; for his harsh language he was demoted and sent out as prefect of Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jian submitted a memorial in protest; for his harsh language he was demoted to prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，就加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was given the additional title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (813) he received the additional title of grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 簡始到郡，開古孟瀆，長四十一里，灌溉沃壤四千余頃，為廉使舉其課績，是有就加之命。

translations.literal: When Jian first arrived in his prefecture, he opened the ancient Meng Canal, forty-one li in length, irrigating more than four thousand qing of fertile land; the investigating commissioner commended his achievements, and this led to the additional appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian first took up his post, he reopened the ancient Meng Canal, forty-one li long, irrigating more than four thousand qing of fertile land; the investigating commissioner commended his achievements, which led to the additional appointment.

sentences.zh: 是歲，征拜為給事中。

translations.literal: That year he was summoned and appointed Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was summoned to court as supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 九年，出為越州刺史、兼御史中丞、浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was sent out as prefect of Yue Prefecture, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief and Zhedong Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (814) he was appointed prefect of Yuezhou, concurrently vice censor-in-chief and Zhedong observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 承李遜抑遏士族、恣縱編戶之後，及簡為政，一皆反之，而農估多受其弊，當時以為兩未可也。

translations.literal: After Li Xun had restrained the gentry clans and indulged the registered households, when Jian took office he reversed everything; yet the farming levies suffered much under him, and at the time people thought neither course was right.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xun had restrained the gentry clans while indulging the registered households, Jian reversed every policy upon taking office; yet the farming levies suffered greatly under him, and contemporaries thought neither man had been right.

sentences.zh: 十二年，入為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he entered court as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (817) he entered court as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 十三年，代崔元略為御史中丞，仍兼戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he replaced Cui Yuanlue as Vice Censor-in-Chief, still concurrently Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (818) he replaced Cui Yuanlue as vice censor-in-chief, while retaining his post as vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 是歲，出為襄州刺史、山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: That year he was sent out as prefect of Xiang Prefecture and military governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was sent out as prefect of Xiangzhou and military governor of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 十四年，敕於谷城縣置群牧，命曰「臨漢監」，令簡充使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an edict established a herd office in Gucheng County, naming it the "Linhan Pasturage," and ordered Jian to serve as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (819) an edict established a herd office in Gucheng County named the "Linhan Pasturage" and ordered Jian to serve as its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 簡奏請均州鄖鄉縣鎮遏使趙潔充本縣令，臺司奏有虧刑典，罰一月俸。

translations.literal: Jian memorialized requesting that Zhao Jie, pacification commissioner of Yunxiang County in Jun Prefecture, be appointed magistrate of that county; the censorate reported that this violated the penal code, and he was fined one month's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Jian memorialized requesting that Zhao Jie, pacification commissioner of Yunxiang County in Junzhou, be appointed magistrate of that county; the censorate ruled this violated the penal code and fined him one month's salary.

sentences.zh: 是歲，改授太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: That year he was reassigned as Senior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with duties at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was reassigned as senior mentor to the heir apparent, with duties at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 十五年，穆宗即位，貶吉州司馬員外置同正員。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when Emperor Muzong took the throne, Jian was demoted to Vice Director of Ji Prefecture, supernumerary with concurrent regular status.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (820), when Emperor Muzong took the throne, Jian was demoted to vice director of Jizhou, supernumerary with concurrent regular status.

sentences.zh: 初，簡在襄陽，以腹心吏陸翰知上都進奏，委以關通中貴。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Jian was in Xiangyang, he had entrusted his trusted clerk Lu Han with submitting memorials to the capital and relied on him to maintain contact with palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Jian was in Xiangyang, he had entrusted his trusted clerk Lu Han with submitting memorials to the capital and relied on him to maintain contact with palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 翰持簡陰事，漸不可制。

translations.literal: Han held Jian's secrets and gradually became uncontrollable.
translations.idiomatic: Han held Jian's secrets and gradually grew beyond control.

sentences.zh: 簡怒，追至州，以土囊殺之，且欲滅口。

translations.literal: Jian, enraged, had him pursued to the prefecture, killed him with a sandbag, and wished to silence all witnesses.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Jian had him pursued to the prefecture, killed him with a sandbag, and tried to silence all witnesses.

sentences.zh: 翰子弟詣闕，進狀訴冤，且告簡贓狀。

translations.literal: Han's younger kinsmen went to the palace, submitted petitions to plead their grievance, and also reported Jian's acts of corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Han's younger kinsmen went to the palace, submitted petitions pleading their grievance, and also reported Jian's acts of corruption.

sentences.zh: 御史臺按驗，獲簡賂吐突承璀錢帛等共計七千余貫匹，事狀明白，故再貶之。

translations.literal: The censorate investigated and found that Jian had bribed Tuhu Chenghui with money and goods totaling more than seven thousand strings and bolts; the facts were clear, and so he was demoted again.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate investigated and found that Jian had bribed Tuhu Chenghui with money and goods totaling more than seven thousand strings and bolts; the facts were clear, and he was demoted again.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年大赦，量移睦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the general amnesty of the first year of Changqing, he was transferred on discretion to prefect of Mu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the general amnesty of the first year of Changqing (821), he was transferred at discretion to prefect of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，移常州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was moved to prefect of Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (822) he was moved to prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，入為太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered court as Senior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with duties at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (823) he entered court as senior mentor to the heir apparent, with duties at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month of that year.

sentences.zh: 簡性俊拔尚義。

translations.literal: Jian's nature was lofty and he esteemed righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was lofty in character and esteemed righteousness.

sentences.zh: 早歲交友先歿者，視其孤，每厚於周恤，議者以為有前輩風。

translations.literal: For friends who had died while he was still young, he looked after their orphans and always treated them with generous support; commentators held that he had the manner of an elder generation.
translations.idiomatic: For friends who had died while he was still young, he looked after their orphans and always treated them generously; commentators held that he had the bearing of an elder generation.

sentences.zh: 然溺於浮圖之教，為儒曹所誚。

translations.literal: Yet he was immersed in Buddhist teachings and was mocked by the Confucian officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was immersed in Buddhist teachings and was mocked by the Confucian officials.

sentences.zh: 胡證

translations.literal: Hu Zheng
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zheng

sentences.zh: 胡證，字啟中，河東人。

translations.literal: Hu Zheng, style name Qizhong, was a native of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zheng, whose style name was Qizhong, was from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父瑱，伯父玫，登進士第。

translations.literal: His father Zhen and his father's elder brother Mei both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen and his father's elder brother Mei both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 證，貞元中繼登科，咸寧王渾瑊辟為河中從事。

translations.literal: Zheng, in the Zhenyuan era, also passed the examination; Prince of Xianning Hun Zhen recruited him as staff officer in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng also passed the examination during the Zhenyuan era; the Prince of Xianning, Hun Zhen, recruited him as a staff officer in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 自殿中侍御史拜韶州刺史，以母年高不可適遠，改授太子舍人。

translations.literal: From Attending Censor he was appointed prefect of Shao Prefecture; because his mother was advanced in years and could not travel far, he was reassigned as Secretary to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: From attending censor he was appointed prefect of Shaozhou; because his mother was advanced in years and could not travel far, he was reassigned as secretary to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 襄陽節度使於頔請為掌書記，檢校祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: Military Governor of Xiangyang Yu Di requested him as chief secretary; he was made Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Rites, acting.
translations.idiomatic: Military governor of Xiangyang Yu Di requested him as chief secretary; he was made acting supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 元和四年，由侍御史歷左司員外郎、長安縣令、戶部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe, from Attending Censor he served successively as Vice Director in the Left Secretariat, magistrate of Chang'an County, and Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhe (809), from attending censor he served successively as vice director in the Left Secretariat, magistrate of Chang'an County, and director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 田弘正以魏博內屬，請除副貳，乃兼御史中丞，充魏博節度副使，仍兼左庶子。

translations.literal: When Tian Hongzheng brought Weibo within the empire, he requested a deputy; Zheng was concurrently made Vice Censor-in-Chief and deputy military governor of Weibo, still concurrently Junior Mentor on the Left.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Hongzheng brought Weibo within the empire, he requested a deputy; Zheng was concurrently made vice censor-in-chief and deputy military governor of Weibo, while still serving as junior mentor on the left.

sentences.zh: 入遷左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He entered court and was promoted to Left Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court and was promoted to left remonstrance grandee.

sentences.zh: 九年，以党項寇邊，以證有安邊才略，乃授單於都護、御史大夫、振武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, because the Tangut tribes raided the border, and because Zheng had talent and strategy for securing the frontier, he was appointed Chief Guardian of the Shanyu, Censor-in-Chief, and military governor of Zhenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (814), because the Tangut tribes raided the border and Zheng possessed talent and strategy for securing the frontier, he was appointed chief guardian of the Shanyu, censor-in-chief, and military governor of Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 前任將帥非統馭之才，邊事曠廢，朝廷故特用證以鎮。

translations.literal: The previous generals lacked the talent to command; border affairs had been neglected, and so the court specially used Zheng to stabilize the region.
translations.idiomatic: The previous generals lacked the talent to command; border affairs had been neglected, and so the court specially appointed Zheng to stabilize the region.

sentences.zh: 十三年，征為金吾大將軍，依前兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was summoned as Grand General of the Imperial Guards, still concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (818) he was summoned as grand general of the imperial guards, still concurrently censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十四年，充京西、京北巡邊使，訪其利害以聞。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he served as frontier inspection commissioner for Jingxi and Jingbei, investigating advantages and disadvantages to report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (819) he served as frontier inspection commissioner for Jingxi and Jingbei, investigating advantages and disadvantages to report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，太和公主出降回紇，詔以本官檢校工部尚書充和親使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing, when Princess Taihe was sent in marriage to the Uyghurs, an edict appointed him, in his existing office, Acting Minister of Works and commissioner for the marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing (821), when Princess Taihe was sent in marriage to the Uyghurs, an edict appointed him, in his existing office, acting minister of works and commissioner for the marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 舊制，以使車出境，有行人私覿之禮，官不能給，召富家子納貲於使者而命之官。

translations.literal: By old regulation, when an envoy's carriage crossed the border there was a private audience gift; the office could not supply it, so wealthy men's sons paid the envoy and were then appointed to office.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation, when an envoy's carriage crossed the border there was a private audience gift that the office could not supply, so wealthy men's sons paid the envoy and were then appointed to office.

sentences.zh: 及證將行，首請厘革，儉受省費，以絕鬻官之門。

translations.literal: When Zheng was about to depart, he first requested reform, accepting frugally and saving expenses to shut the door on selling offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng was about to depart, he first requested reforms, accepting only modest gifts and saving expenses to shut the door on the sale of offices.

sentences.zh: 行及漠南，虜騎繼至，狼心犬態，一日千狀，欲以戎服變革華服，又欲以王姬疾驅徑路。

translations.literal: On reaching the southern desert, barbarian horsemen came in succession; wolfish in heart and doglike in manner, their moods changed a thousand times a day; they wished to change splendid robes into barbarian dress, and also wished to drive the princess at full speed along a direct route.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the southern desert, barbarian horsemen came in succession; wolfish in heart and doglike in manner, their moods changed a thousand times a day. They wished to change splendid robes into barbarian dress and also wished to drive the princess at full speed along a direct route.

sentences.zh: 證抗誌不拔，守漢儀，黜夷法，竟不辱君命。

translations.literal: Zheng stood firm in resolve, upheld Han ritual, and dismissed barbarian ways, and in the end did not disgrace his sovereign's commission.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng stood firm in resolve, upheld Han ritual, and dismissed barbarian ways, and in the end did not disgrace his sovereign's commission.

sentences.zh: 使還，拜工部侍郎。

translations.literal: On returning from his mission he was appointed Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from his mission he was appointed vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 敬宗即位之初，檢校戶部尚書，守京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Jingzong's reign he was made Acting Minister of Revenue and Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Jingzong's reign he was made acting minister of revenue and metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 數月，遷左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: After several months he was transferred to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was transferred to left regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，拜戶部尚書、判度支，上表乞免，願效籓服。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoli era he was appointed Minister of Revenue and Controller of the Treasury, and submitted a memorial requesting to be relieved, wishing to serve in a frontier post.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Baoli era he was appointed minister of revenue and controller of the treasury, and submitted a memorial requesting to be relieved, wishing to serve in a frontier post.

sentences.zh: 二年，檢校兵部尚書、廣州刺史，充嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made Acting Minister of War, prefect of Guang Prefecture, and military governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (826) he was made acting minister of war, prefect of Guangzhou, and military governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，以疾上表求還京師。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, because of illness he submitted a memorial requesting return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe (828), because of illness he submitted a memorial requesting return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月卒於嶺南，時年七十一，廢朝一日，贈左僕射。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year he died in Lingnan at the age of seventy-one; the court suspended audiences for one day and posthumously appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year he died in Lingnan at the age of seventy-one; the court suspended audiences for one day and posthumously appointed him left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 廣州有海之利，貨貝狎至。

translations.literal: Guangzhou had the profits of the sea; goods and treasures arrived in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou enjoyed the profits of the sea; goods and treasures arrived in abundance.

sentences.zh: 證善蓄積，務華侈，厚自奉養，童奴數百，於京城修行裏起第，連亙閭巷。

translations.literal: Zheng was good at accumulating wealth and pursued lavish display, providing richly for himself; he had several hundred household slaves, and in the capital at Xingxing Lane he built a mansion stretching through the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was skilled at accumulating wealth and pursued lavish display, providing richly for himself. He kept several hundred household slaves, and in the capital at Xingxing Lane he built a mansion stretching through the lanes.

sentences.zh: 嶺表奇貨，道途不絕，京邑推為富家。

translations.literal: Exotic goods from beyond the ranges flowed along the roads without cease; the capital regarded him as a wealthy family.
translations.idiomatic: Exotic goods from beyond the ranges flowed along the roads without cease; the capital regarded him as one of its wealthiest families.

sentences.zh: 證素與賈餗善，及李訓事敗，禁軍利其財，稱證子溵匿餗，乃破其家。

translations.literal: Zheng had long been on good terms with Jia Su; when Li Xun's affair failed, the imperial guards coveted his wealth and claimed that Zheng's son Yin had hidden Su, and so his household was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had long been on good terms with Jia Su; when Li Xun's affair failed, the imperial guards coveted his wealth and claimed that Zheng's son Yin had hidden Su, and so his household was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 一日之內，家財並盡。

translations.literal: Within a single day his family wealth was entirely gone.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single day his family wealth was entirely gone.

sentences.zh: 軍人執溵入左軍，仇士良命斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Soldiers seized Yin and took him into the Left Army; Qiu Shiliang ordered him beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers seized Yin and took him into the Left Army; Qiu Shiliang ordered him beheaded as a warning.

sentences.zh: 時溵弟湘為太原從事，忽白晝見綠衣人無首，血流被地，入於室，湘惡之。

translations.literal: At the time Yin's younger brother Xiang was a staff officer in Taiyuan; suddenly in broad daylight he saw a green-robed man without a head, blood soaking the ground, enter the room, and Xiang was horrified.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yin's younger brother Xiang was a staff officer in Taiyuan; suddenly in broad daylight he saw a green-robed man without a head, blood soaking the ground, enter the room, and Xiang was horrified.

sentences.zh: 翌日，溵兇問至，而湘獲免。

translations.literal: The next day news of Yin's violent death arrived, and Xiang was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The next day news of Yin's violent death arrived, and Xiang was spared.

sentences.zh: 崔元略

translations.literal: Cui Yuanlue
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanlue

sentences.zh: 崔元略，博陵人。

translations.literal: Cui Yuanlue was a native of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanlue was from Boling.

sentences.zh: 祖渾之。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Hunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Hunzhi.

sentences.zh: 父儆，貞元中官至尚書左丞。

translations.literal: His father Jing, in the Zhenyuan era, rose to Left Vice Director in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing rose during the Zhenyuan era to left vice director in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 元略舉進士，歷佐使府。

translations.literal: Yuanlue passed the jinshi examination and served successively in regional staff offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlue passed the jinshi examination and served successively in regional staff offices.

sentences.zh: 元和八年，拜殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanhe he was appointed Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanhe (813) he was appointed attending censor.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷刑部郎中、知臺雜事，擢拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Justice and put in charge of censorate miscellaneous affairs, and was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (817) he was transferred to director in the Ministry of Justice and put in charge of censorate miscellaneous affairs, and was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年，以李夷簡自西川征拜御史大夫，乃命元略留司東臺。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe, when Li Yijian was summoned from Xichuan and appointed Censor-in-Chief, Yuanlue was ordered to remain and administer the Eastern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe (818), when Li Yijian was summoned from Xichuan and appointed censor-in-chief, Yuanlue was ordered to remain and administer the Eastern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 尋除京兆少尹，知府事，仍加金紫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made Junior Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, directing prefectural affairs, with the additional title of golden seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made junior metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, directing prefectural affairs, with the additional title of golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 數月，真拜京兆尹。

translations.literal: After several months he was formally appointed Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was formally appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 明年，改左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was changed to left regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，命元略使党項宣撫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Yuanlue was ordered to go as envoy to pacify the Tangut tribes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Yuanlue was ordered to go as envoy to pacify the Tangut tribes.

sentences.zh: 辭疾不行，出為黔南觀察使、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and would not go, and was sent out as Qiannan Observation Commissioner, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and would not go, and was sent out as Qiannan observation commissioner, concurrently vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 初，元略受命使党項，意宰臣以私憾排斥，頗出怨言。

translations.literal: At first, when Yuanlue received the order to go to the Tangut tribes, he believed the chief ministers were excluding him out of private resentment and uttered many complaints.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Yuanlue received the order to go to the Tangut tribes, he believed the chief ministers were excluding him out of private resentment and uttered many complaints.

sentences.zh: 宰相崔植奏曰：「比以聖意切在安撫党項，乃差元略往使。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Cui Zhi memorialized: "Recently, because the sacred intent urgently lay in pacifying the Tangut tribes, Yuanlue was dispatched as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Cui Zhi memorialized: "Recently, because the sacred intent urgently lay in pacifying the Tangut tribes, Yuanlue was dispatched as envoy.

sentences.zh: 受命之後，苦不樂行，言辭之間，頗乖去就。

translations.literal: After receiving the commission he was deeply unwilling to go, and in his words he greatly departed from what was fitting in accepting or refusing office.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving the commission he was deeply unwilling to go, and in his words he greatly departed from what was fitting in accepting or refusing office.

sentences.zh: 豈有身忝重恩，不思報效？

translations.literal: How can one who bears heavy favor not think of repaying it?
translations.idiomatic: How can one who bears heavy favor not think of repaying it?

sentences.zh: 茍非便己，即不肯行。

translations.literal: If it is not convenient for oneself, one simply refuses to go.
translations.idiomatic: If it is not convenient for oneself, one simply refuses to go.

sentences.zh: 須有薄懲，以肅在位，請出為黔中觀察使。」

translations.literal: There must be a light punishment to discipline those in office; I request that he be sent out as Qianzhong Observation Commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: There must be a light punishment to discipline those in office; I request that he be sent out as Qianzhong observation commissioner."

sentences.zh: 初，崔植任吏部郎中，元略任刑部郎中知雜。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Cui Zhi was Director in the Ministry of Personnel, Yuanlue was Director in the Ministry of Justice in charge of miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Cui Zhi was director in the Ministry of Personnel, Yuanlue was director in the Ministry of Justice in charge of miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 時中丞改京兆尹，物議以植有風憲之望。

translations.literal: At the time the vice censor-in-chief was changed to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao; public opinion held that Zhi had the promise of censorial integrity.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the vice censor-in-chief was changed to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao; public opinion held that Zhi had the promise of censorial integrity.

sentences.zh: 元略因入閣，妄稱植失儀，命御史彈之。

translations.literal: Yuanlue, upon entering the audience hall, falsely claimed that Zhi had lost decorum and ordered censors to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlue, upon entering the audience hall, falsely claimed that Zhi had lost decorum and ordered censors to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 時二人皆進擬為中丞，中旨果授元略，植深銜之。

translations.literal: At the time both men were advanced as candidates for vice censor-in-chief; the imperial order indeed appointed Yuanlue, and Zhi deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time both men were advanced as candidates for vice censor-in-chief; the imperial order indeed appointed Yuanlue, and Zhi deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 及植為相，元略以左散騎常侍使於党項；

translations.literal: When Zhi became chief minister, Yuanlue, as Left Regular Attendant, was sent to the Tangut tribes;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi became chief minister, Yuanlue, as left regular attendant, was sent to the Tangut tribes;

sentences.zh: 元略意植之見排，辭疾不行。

translations.literal: Yuanlue believed Zhi was excluding him and pleaded illness and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlue believed Zhi was excluding him and pleaded illness and would not go.

sentences.zh: 被譴出。

translations.literal: He was censured and sent out.
translations.idiomatic: He was censured and sent out.

sentences.zh: 逾年，轉鄂州刺史、鄂嶽都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to prefect of E Prefecture and Commander of the E-Yue Defense and Observation Command.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was transferred to prefect of Ezhou and commander of the E-Yue defense and observation command.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年，入為大理卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changqing he entered court as Chief Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Changqing (824) he entered court as chief minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 敬宗即位，復為京兆尹，尋兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, he again became Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, and soon was concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, he again became metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, and soon was concurrently censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 以誤征畿甸經赦免放緡錢萬七千貫，為侍御史蕭澈彈劾。

translations.literal: For mistakenly collecting more than seventeen thousand strings of exempted tax money from the capital region after an amnesty, he was impeached by Attending Censor Xiao Che.
translations.idiomatic: For mistakenly collecting more than seventeen thousand strings of exempted tax money from the capital region after an amnesty, he was impeached by attending censor Xiao Che.

sentences.zh: 有詔刑部郎中趙元亮、大理正元從質、侍御史溫造充三司覆理。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhao Yuanliang, Director in the Ministry of Justice, Yuan Congzhi, Senior Adjudicator in the Court of Judicial Review, and Attending Censor Wen Zao to conduct a three-office review.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zhao Yuanliang, director in the Ministry of Justice, Yuan Congzhi, senior adjudicator in the Court of Judicial Review, and attending censor Wen Zao to conduct a three-office review.

sentences.zh: 元略有中助，止於削兼大夫。

translations.literal: Yuanlue had support within the palace and was only stripped of his concurrent post as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlue had support within the palace and was only stripped of his concurrent post as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 初，元略有宰相望，及是事，望益減。

translations.literal: Earlier Yuanlue had the prospect of becoming chief minister; after this affair his prospects greatly diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yuanlue had the prospect of becoming chief minister; after this affair his prospects greatly diminished.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年，遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoli he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoli (825) he was transferred to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 議者以元略版圖之拜，出於宣授。

translations.literal: Commentators held that Yuanlue's appointment to the Ministry of Revenue came from an edict of direct appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that Yuanlue's appointment to the Ministry of Revenue came from an edict of direct appointment.

sentences.zh: 時諫官有疏，指言內常侍崔潭峻方有權寵，元略以諸父事之，故雖被彈劾，而遽遷顯要。

translations.literal: At the time remonstrance officials submitted memorials pointing out that Palace Attendant Cui Tanjun then held power and favor, and Yuanlue treated him as a paternal uncle; therefore, though impeached, he was swiftly moved to an eminent post.
translations.idiomatic: At the time remonstrance officials submitted memorials pointing out that palace attendant Cui Tanjun then held power and favor, and Yuanlue treated him as a paternal uncle; therefore, though impeached, he was swiftly moved to an eminent post.

sentences.zh: 元略亦上章自辨，且曰：「一昨府縣條疏，臺司舉劾，孤立無黨，謗言益彰，不謂詔出宸衷，恩延望外。

translations.literal: Yuanlue also submitted a memorial in his own defense, saying: "Recently the prefecture and county submitted reports and the censorate impeached me; isolated and without faction, slander grew all the more, and I did not expect an edict from the imperial heart extending favor beyond what I had hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlue also submitted a memorial in his own defense, saying: "Recently the prefecture and county submitted reports and the censorate impeached me; isolated and without faction, slander grew all the more, and I did not expect an edict from the imperial heart extending favor beyond what I had hoped for.

sentences.zh: 處南宮之重位，列左戶之清班，豈臣庸虛，敢自幹冒。

translations.literal: To hold the weighty post of the Southern Palace and stand in the pure ranks of the Left Household—how could I, a mediocre man, dare presume upon myself?
translations.idiomatic: To hold the weighty post of the Southern Palace and stand in the pure ranks of the Left Household—how could I, a mediocre man, dare presume upon myself?

sentences.zh: 天心所擇，雖驚特進之恩；

translations.literal: What Heaven chooses, though it startles me with extraordinary advancement;
translations.idiomatic: What Heaven chooses, though it startles me with extraordinary advancement;

sentences.zh: 眾口相非，乃致因緣之說。」

translations.literal: the mouths of the multitude speak against me, and so the talk of connections arises."
translations.idiomatic: the mouths of the multitude speak against me, and so the talk of connections arises."

sentences.zh: 詔答之曰：「朕所命官，豈非公選？

translations.literal: The edict answered: "The officials I appoint—are they not chosen by public selection?
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered: "The officials I appoint—are they not chosen by public selection?

sentences.zh: 卿能稱職，奚恤人言！」

translations.literal: If you can fulfill your duties, why worry about what people say!"
translations.idiomatic: If you can fulfill your duties, why worry about what people say!"

sentences.zh: 然元略終不能逃父事潭峻之名。

translations.literal: Yet Yuanlue in the end could not escape the name of treating Tanjun as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yuanlue in the end could not escape the name of treating Tanjun as a father.

sentences.zh: 寶歷二年四月，京兆府以元略前任尹日為橋道使，造東渭橋時，被本典鄭位、判官鄭復虛長物價，擡估給用，不還人工價直，率斂工匠破用，計贓二萬一千七百九貫。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Baoli, the metropolitan government reported that when Yuanlue had formerly been metropolitan governor he had served as bridge-road commissioner in building the East Wei Bridge; the chief clerk Zheng Wei and aide Zheng Fu had falsely inflated prices, overestimated supplies, failed to repay labor costs, and extorted craftsmen for losses, totaling more than twenty-one thousand seven hundred and ninety strings in illicit gains.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Baoli (826), the metropolitan government reported that when Yuanlue had formerly been metropolitan governor he had served as bridge-road commissioner in building the East Wei Bridge; the chief clerk Zheng Wei and aide Zheng Fu had falsely inflated prices, overestimated supplies, failed to repay labor costs, and extorted craftsmen for losses, totaling more than twenty-one thousand seven hundred and ninety strings in illicit gains.

sentences.zh: 敕云：「元略不能檢下，有涉慢官，罰一月俸料。」

translations.literal: The edict read: "Yuanlue could not keep his subordinates in check and was involved in slighting official duty; he is fined one month's salary."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Yuanlue could not keep his subordinates in check and was involved in slighting official duty; he is fined one month's salary."

sentences.zh: 時劉棲楚自為京兆尹，有覬覦相位之意。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Qichu, who had become Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, harbored ambitions for the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Qichu, who had become metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, harbored ambitions for the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 元賂方在次對，又多遊裴度門，棲楚恐礙己，以計摧之，乃按舉山陵時錢物以汙之。

translations.literal: Yuanlue was then in the next audience and often visited Pei Du's house; Qichu, fearing he would obstruct him, used a stratagem to crush him and investigated the funds for the imperial tomb as corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlue was then in the next audience and often visited Pei Du's house; Qichu, fearing he would obstruct him, used a stratagem to crush him and investigated the funds for the imperial tomb as corruption.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，轉戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe (829) he was transferred to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 四年，判度支。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he controlled the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (830) he controlled the treasury.

sentences.zh: 五年，檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (831) he was made acting minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 出為東都留守、畿汝等防禦使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Eastern Capital Guardian and Defense Commissioner for Ji and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Eastern Capital guardian and defense commissioner for Ji and Ru.

sentences.zh: 是歲，又遷滑州刺史、義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: That year he was again transferred to prefect of Hua Prefecture and military governor of Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was again transferred to prefect of Huazhou and military governor of Yicheng Army.

sentences.zh: 十二月卒，廢朝三日，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died; audiences were suspended for three days, and he was posthumously appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month; audiences were suspended for three days, and he was posthumously appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子鉉。

translations.literal: His son Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan.

sentences.zh: 鉉，字台碩，登進士第。

translations.literal: Xuan, style name Taisuo, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, whose style name was Taisuo, passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 三辟諸侯府，荊南、西蜀掌書記。

translations.literal: He was three times recruited to regional staff offices and served as chief secretary in Jingnan and Xishu.
translations.idiomatic: He was three times recruited to regional staff offices and served as chief secretary in Jingnan and Xishu.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，入為左拾遺，再遷員外郎，知制誥，召入翰林，充學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang he entered court as Left Remonstrance Supplementer, was promoted twice to Supervising Secretary, drafted edicts, was summoned into the Hanlin Academy, and served as academician.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huichang (841) he entered court as left remonstrance supplementer, was promoted twice to supervising secretary, drafted edicts, was summoned into the Hanlin Academy, and served as academician.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部侍郎承旨。

translations.literal: He was promoted successively to Vice Minister of Revenue with drafting authority.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted successively to vice minister of revenue with drafting authority.

sentences.zh: 會昌末，以本官同平章事。

translations.literal: At the end of Huichang, in his existing office he became Associate Chief Minister of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Huichang, in his existing office he became associate chief minister of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 為同列李德裕所嫉，罷相，為陜虢觀察使、檢校刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was envied by his colleague Li Deyu, was removed as chief minister, and became Shaan-Guo Observation Commissioner and Acting Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was envied by his colleague Li Deyu, was removed as chief minister, and became Shaan-Guo observation commissioner and acting minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，遷檢校兵部尚書、河中尹、博陵縣開國子，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, he was transferred to Acting Minister of War, Governor of Hezhong, and Baron of Boling County with an estate of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, he was transferred to acting minister of war, governor of Hezhong, and baron of Boling County with an estate of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 大中三年，召拜禦中大夫，尋加正議大夫、中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong he was summoned and appointed Supervisory Censor, and soon was given the additional titles of Regular Grand Master of the Right and Vice Director of the Secretariat, Associate Chief Minister of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dazhong (849) he was summoned and appointed supervisory censor, and soon was given the additional titles of regular grand master of the right and vice director of the Secretariat, associate chief minister of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷金紫光祿大夫，守左僕射、門下侍郎、太清宮使、弘文館大學士、博陵縣開國公，食邑至二千戶。

translations.literal: He was promoted successively to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Commissioner of the Great Pure Palace, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, and Duke of Boling County with an estate increased to two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted successively to grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon, left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, vice director of the Secretariat, commissioner of the Great Pure Palace, grand academician of the Hongwen Hall, and duke of Boling County with an estate increased to two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 七年，以館中學士崔彖、薛逢等撰《續會要》四十卷，獻之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, together with academicians Cui Luan and Xue Feng and others in the hall, he compiled forty juan of the Continued Institutional Compendium and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (853), together with academicians Cui Luan and Xue Feng and others in the hall, he compiled forty juan of the Continued Institutional Compendium and presented it.

sentences.zh: 九年，檢校司徒、揚州大都督長史，進封魏國公、淮南節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was made Acting Minister of the Imperial Clan, Chief Regional Governor of Yang Prefecture, was advanced to Duke of Wei, and became military governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (855) he was made acting minister of the imperial clan, chief regional governor of Yangzhou, was advanced to duke of Wei, and became military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 宣宗於太液亭賦詩宴餞，有「七載秉鈞調四序」之句，儒者榮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong, at Taiye Pavilion, composed a poem for a farewell banquet with the line "Seven years holding the balance, harmonizing the four seasons," and Confucian scholars took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong, at Taiye Pavilion, composed a poem for a farewell banquet with the line "Seven years holding the balance, harmonizing the four seasons," and Confucian scholars took it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，移鎮襄州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he was transferred to govern Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiantong (860) he was transferred to govern Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸通八年，徐州戍將龐勛自桂管擅還，道途剽掠。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xiantong, Pang Xun, garrison commander of Xuzhou, returned without authorization from Guiguan and plundered along the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xiantong (867), Pang Xun, garrison commander of Xuzhou, returned without authorization from Guiguan and plundered along the road.

sentences.zh: 鉉時為荊南節度，聞徐州軍至湖南，盡率州兵，點募丁壯，分扼江、湘要害，欲盡擒之。

translations.literal: Xuan was then military governor of Jingnan; hearing that the Xuzhou army had reached Hunan, he mustered all the prefectural troops, conscripted able-bodied men, and divided them to hold the key points of the Yangtze and Xiang rivers, intending to capture them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was then military governor of Jingnan; hearing that the Xuzhou army had reached Hunan, he mustered all the prefectural troops, conscripted able-bodied men, and divided them to hold the key points of the Yangtze and Xiang rivers, intending to capture them all.

sentences.zh: 徐寇聞之，逾嶺自江西、淮右北渡，朝議壯之。

translations.literal: When the Xuzhou raiders heard of it, they crossed the ranges by Jiangxi and Huaiyou and crossed north; court opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuzhou raiders heard of it, they crossed the ranges by Jiangxi and Huaiyou and crossed north; court opinion praised him.

sentences.zh: 卒於江陵。

translations.literal: He died at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 子沆、汀、潭、沂。

translations.literal: His sons Hang, Ting, Tan, and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Hang, Ting, Tan, and Yi.

sentences.zh: 沆，登進士第，官至員外郎，知制誥，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: Hang passed the jinshi examination, rose to Supervising Secretary, drafted edicts, and was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Hang passed the jinshi examination, rose to supervising secretary, drafted edicts, and was appointed secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 坐事貶循州司戶。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to Registrar of Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was demoted to registrar of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾符初，復拜舍人，尋遷禮部侍郎，典貢舉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu he was again appointed Drafter, and soon was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and put in charge of the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianfu (874) he was again appointed drafter, and soon was transferred to vice minister of rites and put in charge of the examinations.

sentences.zh: 選名士十數人，多至卿相。

translations.literal: He selected more than ten men of reputation, many of whom later reached chief ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: He selected more than ten men of reputation, many of whom later reached chief ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 乾符末，本官同平章事。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianfu, in his existing office he became Associate Chief Minister of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qianfu, in his existing office he became associate chief minister of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 遇京國盜據，從駕不及而卒。

translations.literal: When bandits seized the capital he could not follow the imperial procession and died.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits seized the capital he could not follow the imperial procession and died.

sentences.zh: 沂後官亦隆顯。

translations.literal: Yi later also rose to eminent office.
translations.idiomatic: Yi later also rose to eminent office.

sentences.zh: 元略弟元受、元式、元儒。

translations.literal: Yuanlue's younger brothers Yuanshou, Yuanshi, and Yuanru.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlue's younger brothers Yuanshou, Yuanshi, and Yuanru.

sentences.zh: 元受登進士第，高陵尉，直史館。

translations.literal: Yuanshou passed the jinshi examination, was captain of Gaoling, and served in the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshou passed the jinshi examination, was captain of Gaoling, and served in the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 元和初，於臯謨為河北行營糧料使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, he was grain commissioner for Yu Gao's Hebei campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe, he was grain commissioner for Yu Gao's Hebei campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 元受與韋岵、薛巽、王湘等皆為臯謨判官，分督供饋。

translations.literal: Yuanshou, together with Wei Gu, Xue Xun, and Wang Xiang, all served as aides to Gao and separately supervised supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshou, together with Wei Gu, Xue Xun, and Wang Xiang, all served as aides to Gao and separately supervised supplies.

sentences.zh: 既罷兵，或以臯謨隱沒贓罪，除名賜死。

translations.literal: After the troops were dismissed, some people charged that Gao had concealed corrupt gains; he was stripped of office and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: After the troops were dismissed, some people charged that Gao had concealed corrupt gains; he was stripped of office and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 元受從坐，皆逐嶺表，竟坎壈不達而卒。

translations.literal: Yuanshou was implicated, and all were banished beyond the ranges; he ended in hardship without advancement and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshou was implicated, and all were banished beyond the ranges; he ended in hardship without advancement and died.

sentences.zh: 子鈞、铏、銖相繼登進士第，辟諸侯府。

translations.literal: His sons Jun, Xing, and Zhu passed the jinshi examination in succession and were recruited to regional staff offices.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Jun, Xing, and Zhu passed the jinshi examination in succession and were recruited to regional staff offices.

sentences.zh: 元式，會昌三年檢校左散騎常侍、河中尹、河中晉絳觀察使。

translations.literal: Yuanshi, in the third year of Huichang, was made Acting Left Regular Attendant, Governor of Hezhong, and Hezhong-Jin-Guo Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi, in the third year of Huichang (843), was made acting left regular attendant, governor of Hezhong, and Hezhong-Jin-Guo observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，檢校禮部尚書、太原尹、北都留守、河東節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Acting Minister of Rites, Governor of Taiyuan, Northern Capital Guardian, and Hedong Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (844) he was made acting minister of rites, governor of Taiyuan, northern capital guardian, and Hedong military governor.

sentences.zh: 六年，入為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he entered court as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (846) he entered court as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 宣宗朝領度支，以本官同平章事。

translations.literal: In the Xuanzong reign he controlled the treasury and, in his existing office, became Associate Chief Minister of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xuanzong reign he controlled the treasury and, in his existing office, became associate chief minister of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 元儒，元和五年登進士第。

translations.literal: Yuanru passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanru passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Yuanhe (810).

sentences.zh: 元式子鍇，仕至京兆尹。

translations.literal: Yuanshi's son Kai rose to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi's son Kai rose to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 杜元穎

translations.literal: Du Yuanping
translations.idiomatic: Du Yuanping

sentences.zh: 杜元穎，萊公如晦裔孫也。

translations.literal: Du Yuanping was a descendant of Duke Ruhui of Lai.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yuanping was a descendant of Duke Ruhui of Lai.

sentences.zh: 父佐，官卑。

translations.literal: His father Zuo held a low office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zuo held a low office.

sentences.zh: 元穎，貞元末進士登第，再辟使府。

translations.literal: Yuanping, at the end of the Zhenyuan era, passed the jinshi examination and was twice recruited to regional staff offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanping, at the end of the Zhenyuan era, passed the jinshi examination and was twice recruited to regional staff offices.

sentences.zh: 元和中為左拾遺、右補闕，召入翰林，充學士。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he was Left Remonstrance Supplementer and Right Remonstrance Supplementer, was summoned into the Hanlin Academy, and served as academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era he was left remonstrance supplementer and right remonstrance supplementer, was summoned into the Hanlin Academy, and served as academician.

sentences.zh: 手筆敏速，憲宗稱之。

translations.literal: His hand was quick at writing; Emperor Xianzong praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His hand was quick at writing; Emperor Xianzong praised him.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟平，以書詔之勤，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanji was pacified, for his diligence in drafting edicts he was granted the crimson fish bag.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji was pacified, for his diligence in drafting edicts he was granted the crimson fish bag.

sentences.zh: 轉司勛員外郎，知制誥。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel and drafted edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel and drafted edicts.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，召對思政殿，賜金紫，超拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, he was summoned to the Hall of Reflecting on Governance, granted golden seal and purple ribbon, and promoted out of turn to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, he was summoned to the Hall of Reflecting on Governance, granted golden seal and purple ribbon, and promoted out of turn to secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，拜戶部侍郎承旨。

translations.literal: That winter he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue with drafting authority.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was appointed vice minister of revenue with drafting authority.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年三月，以本官同平章事，加上柱國、建安男。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Changqing, in his existing office he became Associate Chief Minister of State Affairs, with the additional titles of Pillar of State and Baron of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Changqing (821), in his existing office he became associate chief minister of state affairs, with the additional titles of pillar of state and baron of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 元穎自穆宗登極，自補闕至侍郎，不周歲居輔相之地。

translations.literal: From the time Muzong ascended the throne, Yuanping rose from remonstrance supplementer to vice minister in less than a year and occupied the place of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Muzong ascended the throne, Yuanping rose from remonstrance supplementer to vice minister in less than a year and occupied the place of chief minister.

sentences.zh: 辭臣速達，未有如元穎之比也。

translations.literal: Among remonstrance officials who rose swiftly, none compared with Yuanping.
translations.idiomatic: Among remonstrance officials who rose swiftly, none compared with Yuanping.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，帶平章事出鎮蜀州，穆宗禦安福門臨餞。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year he went out to govern Shu Prefecture with chief ministerial rank; Muzong, at Anfu Gate, came out to bid him farewell.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year (823) he went out to govern Shuzhou with chief ministerial rank; Muzong, at Anfu Gate, came out to bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 昭湣即位，童心多僻，務為奢侈，而元穎求蜀中珍異玩好之具，貢奉相繼，以固恩寵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaomin took the throne, childish and eccentric, he pursued extravagance, and Yuanping sought rare and curious treasures of Shu to present in succession, thereby securing favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaomin took the throne, childish and eccentric, he pursued extravagance, and Yuanping sought rare and curious treasures of Shu to present in succession, thereby securing favor.

sentences.zh: 以故箕斂刻削，工作無虛日，軍民嗟怨，流聞於朝。

translations.literal: Therefore he levied and squeezed without cease, and construction work never ceased for a day; soldiers and people groaned in resentment, and the news spread to court.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he levied and squeezed without cease, and construction work never ceased for a day; soldiers and people groaned in resentment, and the news spread to court.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，南詔蠻攻陷戎、巂等州，徑犯成都。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe, the Nanzhao barbarians attacked and captured Rong and Xi and other prefectures and advanced straight against Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe (829), the Nanzhao barbarians attacked and captured Rong and Xi and other prefectures and advanced straight against Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 兵及城下，一無備擬，方率左右固牙城而已。

translations.literal: When the troops reached beneath the walls there was not a single preparation; he merely led his attendants to hold the inner citadel.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops reached beneath the walls there was not a single preparation; he merely led his attendants to hold the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 蠻兵大掠蜀城玉帛、子女、工巧之具而去。

translations.literal: The barbarian troops greatly plundered the jade, silk, women, and skilled craftsmen of Shu city and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian troops greatly plundered the jade, silk, women, and skilled craftsmen of Shu city and departed.

sentences.zh: 是時，蠻三道而來，東道攻梓州，郭釗禦之而退。

translations.literal: At that time the barbarians came by three routes; the eastern route attacked Zizhou and was repelled by Guo Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the barbarians came by three routes; the eastern route attacked Zizhou and was repelled by Guo Zhao.

sentences.zh: 時元穎幾陷，賴郭釗擊敗其眾，方還。

translations.literal: At the time Yuanping was nearly lost; only because Guo Zhao defeated their forces did they return.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuanping was nearly lost; only because Guo Zhao defeated their forces did they return.

sentences.zh: 蠻驅蜀人至大渡河，謂之曰；

translations.literal: The barbarians drove the people of Shu to the Great Crossing River and said to them:
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians drove the people of Shu to the Great Crossing River and said to them:

sentences.zh: 「此南吾境，放爾哭別鄉國。」

translations.literal: "This to the south is our territory; I release you to weep and bid farewell to your homeland."
translations.idiomatic: "This to the south is our territory; I release you to weep and bid farewell to your homeland."

sentences.zh: 數萬士女，一時慟哭，風日為之慘淒。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of men and women wept at once, and wind and sun turned bleak and mournful.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of men and women wept at once, and wind and sun turned bleak and mournful.

sentences.zh: 哭已，赴水而死者千余。

translations.literal: After weeping they threw themselves into the water, and more than a thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: After weeping they threw themselves into the water, and more than a thousand died.

sentences.zh: 怨毒之聲，累年不息。

translations.literal: The sound of bitter resentment did not cease for years.
translations.idiomatic: The sound of bitter resentment did not cease for years.

sentences.zh: 蠻首領泬顛遣人上表曰：「蠻軍比修職貢，遽敢侵邊？

translations.literal: The barbarian leader Juedian sent someone to submit a memorial: "The barbarian army has lately maintained tribute duties—how dare they suddenly invade the border?
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian leader Juedian sent someone to submit a memorial: "The barbarian army has lately maintained tribute duties—how dare they suddenly invade the border?

sentences.zh: 但杜元穎不恤三軍，令入蠻疆作賊；

translations.literal: But Du Yuanping did not care for the three armies and sent them into barbarian territory to act as bandits;
translations.idiomatic: But Du Yuanping did not care for the three armies and sent them into barbarian territory to act as bandits;

sentences.zh: 移文報彼，都不見信。

translations.literal: when we sent documents informing them, they paid no heed at all.
translations.idiomatic: when we sent documents informing them, they paid no heed at all.

sentences.zh: 故蜀部軍人，繼為鄉導，蓋蜀人怨苦之深，祈我此行，誅虐帥也。

translations.literal: Therefore the soldiers of Shu in succession served as local guides, for the people of Shu were deeply resentful and prayed for this campaign to punish the cruel commander.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the soldiers of Shu in succession served as local guides, for the people of Shu were deeply resentful and prayed for this campaign to punish the cruel commander.

sentences.zh: 誅之不遂，無以慰蜀士之心，願陛下誅之。」

translations.literal: If we cannot execute him, we cannot comfort the hearts of the men of Shu; I beg Your Majesty to execute him."
translations.idiomatic: If we cannot execute him, we cannot comfort the hearts of the men of Shu; I beg Your Majesty to execute him."

sentences.zh: 監軍小使張士謙至，備言元穎之咎。

translations.literal: Supervisory Attendant Zhang Shiqian arrived and fully reported Yuanping's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory attendant Zhang Shiqian arrived and fully reported Yuanping's faults.

sentences.zh: 坐貶循州司馬，判官崔璜連州司馬，紇幹臮郢州長史，盧並唐州司馬，皆以佐元穎無狀也。

translations.literal: For this Yuanping was demoted to Vice Director of Xun Prefecture; his aide Cui Huang to Vice Director of Lian Prefecture; his aide Heganzhi to Chief of Ying Prefecture; and his aide Lu Bing to Vice Director of Tang Prefecture—all because they had assisted Yuanping in misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: For this Yuanping was demoted to vice director of Xunzhou; his aide Cui Huang to vice director of Lianzhou; his aide Heganzhi to chief of Yingzhou; and his aide Lu Bing to vice director of Tangzhou—all because they had assisted Yuanping in misconduct.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒於貶所。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died at his place of demotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (832) he died at his place of demotion.

sentences.zh: 臨終，上表乞贈官，贈湖州刺史。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he submitted a memorial requesting posthumous appointment and was granted Prefect of Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he submitted a memorial requesting posthumous appointment and was granted prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 元穎弟元絳，位終太子賓客。

translations.literal: Yuanping's younger brother Yuanjiang ended as Senior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanping's younger brother Yuanjiang ended as senior mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 絳子審權，位至宰相，自有傳。

translations.literal: Jiang's son Shenquan rose to chief minister and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang's son Shenquan rose to chief minister and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 崔弘禮

translations.literal: Cui Hongli
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hongli

sentences.zh: 崔弘禮，字從周，博陵人。

translations.literal: Cui Hongli, style name Congzhou, was a native of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hongli, whose style name was Congzhou, was from Boling.

sentences.zh: 北齊懷遠之七伐孫。

translations.literal: He was the seventh-generation descendant of Qifa of the Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was the seventh-generation descendant of Qifa of the Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 祖育，常州江陰令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu was magistrate of Jiangyin in Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu was magistrate of Jiangyin in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 父孚，湖州長城令。

translations.literal: His father Fu was magistrate of Changcheng in Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu was magistrate of Changcheng in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘禮風貌魁偉，磊落有大志。

translations.literal: Hongli's bearing was imposing and lofty; he was open and magnanimous and had great ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Hongli's bearing was imposing and lofty; he was open and magnanimous and had great ambitions.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，累佐蕃府，官至侍御史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served successively in frontier staff offices, and rose to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served successively in frontier staff offices, and rose to attending censor.

sentences.zh: 元和中，呂元膺為東都留守，以弘禮為從事。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Lü Yuanying was Eastern Capital Guardian and took Hongli as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era, Lü Yuanying was Eastern Capital guardian and took Hongli as staff officer.

sentences.zh: 時淮西吳少陽初死，吳元濟阻兵拒命，山東反側之徒，為之影援；

translations.literal: At the time Wu Shaoyang of Huainan had just died, and Wu Yuanji held the army and defied orders; rebels in the east who wavered gave them covert support;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wu Shaoyang of Huainan had just died, and Wu Yuanji held the army and defied orders; rebels in the east who wavered gave them covert support;

sentences.zh: 東結李師道，謀襲東洛，以脅朝廷。

translations.literal: in the east they allied with Li Shidao and plotted to strike the Eastern Capital to coerce the court.
translations.idiomatic: in the east they allied with Li Shidao and plotted to strike the Eastern Capital to coerce the court.

sentences.zh: 弘禮為元膺籌畫，部分兵眾，以固東都，卒亦無患。

translations.literal: Hongli planned for Yuanying, deploying troops to secure the Eastern Capital, and in the end there was no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Hongli planned for Yuanying, deploying troops to secure the Eastern Capital, and in the end there was no trouble.

sentences.zh: 累除汾州、棣州刺史。

translations.literal: He was successively appointed prefect of Fen and Di.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively appointed prefect of Fenzhou and Dizhou.

sentences.zh: 會田弘正請入覲，請副使，乃授弘禮衛州刺史，充魏博節度副使，歷鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: When Tian Hongzheng requested to come to court, he asked for a deputy; Hongli was then appointed prefect of Wei Prefecture and deputy military governor of Weibo, and later served as prefect of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Hongzheng requested to come to court, he asked for a deputy; Hongli was then appointed prefect of Weizhou and deputy military governor of Weibo, and later served as prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: b####長慶元年，劉總入覲，張弘靖移鎮范陽，復加弘禮檢校左散騎常侍，充幽州盧龍軍節度副使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing, when Liu Zong came to court and Zhang Hongjing was transferred to govern Fanyang, Hongli was again made Acting Left Regular Attendant and deputy military governor of Youzhou and Lulong Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changqing (821), when Liu Zong came to court and Zhang Hongjing was transferred to govern Fanyang, Hongli was again made acting left regular attendant and deputy military governor of Youzhou and Lulong Army.

sentences.zh: 未及境，幽、鎮兵亂，改為絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Before he reached the border, the troops of You and Zhen mutinied, and he was changed to prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached the border, the troops of You and Zhen mutinied, and he was changed to prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，汴州李絺反，急詔追弘禮為河南尹、兼御史大夫、東都畿汝都防禦副使。

translations.literal: The next year, when Li Chi rebelled at Bian Prefecture, an urgent edict recalled Hongli as Governor of Henan, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Deputy Defense Commissioner for the Eastern Capital and Ji and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Li Chi rebelled at Bianzhou, an urgent edict recalled Hongli as governor of Henan, concurrently censor-in-chief and deputy defense commissioner for the Eastern Capital and Ji and Ru.

sentences.zh: 絺平，遷河陽節度使。

translations.literal: When Chi was pacified, Hongli was transferred to military governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Chi was pacified, Hongli was transferred to military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 整練戈矛，頗壯戎備。

translations.literal: He drilled spears and halberds and greatly strengthened frontier defenses.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled spears and halberds and greatly strengthened frontier defenses.

sentences.zh: 又上言請於秦渠下辟荒田三百頃，歲收粟二萬斛，詔皆從之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting that three hundred qing of wasteland be opened below the Qin Canal, yielding twenty thousand hu of grain each year; the edicts all approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized requesting that three hundred qing of wasteland be opened below the Qin Canal, yielding twenty thousand hu of grain each year; the edicts all approved.

sentences.zh: 以疾連表請代。

translations.literal: Because of illness he submitted successive memorials requesting replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness he submitted successive memorials requesting replacement.

sentences.zh: 數歲，拜檢校戶部尚書、華州刺史。

translations.literal: After several years he was appointed Acting Minister of Revenue and Governor of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was appointed acting minister of revenue and governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 會天平軍節度使烏重胤卒，朝廷難其人，復以弘禮為天平軍節度使，仍詔即日乘遞赴鎮。

translations.literal: When Military Governor of Tianping Wu Chongyin died, the court found no suitable man and again appointed Hongli military governor of Tianping Army, with an edict ordering him to set out that very day by express relay.
translations.idiomatic: When military governor of Tianping Wu Chongyin died, the court found no suitable man and again appointed Hongli military governor of Tianping Army, with an edict ordering him to set out that very day by express relay.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，就加檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, he was given the additional title of Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, he was given the additional title of acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 理鄆三載，改授東都留守，仍遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: After governing Yan for three years he was reassigned as Eastern Capital Guardian and transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After governing Yan for three years he was reassigned as Eastern Capital guardian and transferred to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 詔赴闕，以疾未至。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to come to court, but because of illness he did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to come to court, but because of illness he did not arrive.

sentences.zh: 太和四年十月，復除留守。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Taihe he was again appointed guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Taihe (830) he was again appointed guardian.

sentences.zh: 是歲十二月卒，年六十四，贈司空。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year he died at the age of sixty-four and was posthumously appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of that year he died at the age of sixty-four and was posthumously appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 弘禮少時，專以倜儻意氣自任；

translations.literal: In his youth Hongli relied entirely on unconventional spirit and bold resolve;
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Hongli relied entirely on unconventional spirit and bold resolve;

sentences.zh: 通涉兵書，留心軍旋之要，用此累更選用，歷踐籓鎮。

translations.literal: he studied military books thoroughly and attended to the essentials of armies on campaign, and through this was repeatedly selected and promoted, serving successively in frontier commands.
translations.idiomatic: he studied military books thoroughly and attended to the essentials of armies on campaign, and through this was repeatedly selected and promoted, serving successively in frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 所居無可尚之績，雖繕完有素，然善治生蓄積，物議少之。

translations.literal: Where he served there was no outstanding achievement to praise; though he maintained defenses well by habit, he was skilled at managing livelihood and accumulating wealth, and public opinion thought little of him.
translations.idiomatic: Where he served there was no outstanding achievement to praise; though he maintained defenses well by habit, he was skilled at managing livelihood and accumulating wealth, and public opinion thought little of him.

sentences.zh: 李虞仲

translations.literal: Li Yuzhong
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuzhong

sentences.zh: 李虞仲，字見之，趙郡人。

translations.literal: Li Yuzhong, style name Jianzhi, was a native of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuzhong, whose style name was Jianzhi, was from Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖震，大理丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was aide in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen was aide in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 父端，登進士第，工詩。

translations.literal: His father Duan passed the jinshi examination and was skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Duan passed the jinshi examination and was skilled in poetry.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，與韓翃、錢起、盧綸等文詠唱和，馳名都下，號「大歷十才子」。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, together with Han Hong, Qian Qi, Lu Lun, and others he exchanged literary verses in song; he became famous in the capital and was called the "Ten Talents of the Dali Era."
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era, together with Han Hong, Qian Qi, Lu Lun, and others he exchanged literary verses in song; he became famous in the capital and was called the "Ten Talents of the Dali Era."

sentences.zh: 時郭尚父少子曖尚代宗女升平公主，賢明有才思，尤喜詩人，而端等十人，多在曖之門下。

translations.literal: At the time Guo Shangfu's youngest son Ai married Princess Shengping of Emperor Daizong; intelligent and talented, she especially loved poets, and Duan and the other ten men were mostly in Ai's household.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Guo Shangfu's youngest son Ai married Princess Shengping of Emperor Daizong; intelligent and talented, she especially loved poets, and Duan and the other ten men were mostly in Ai's household.

sentences.zh: 每宴集賦詩，公主坐視簾中，詩之美者，賞百縑。

translations.literal: Whenever they gathered for banquets and composed poems, the princess sat behind the curtain watching; for the finest poems she rewarded a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they gathered for banquets and composed poems, the princess sat behind the curtain watching; for the finest poems she rewarded a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 曖因拜官，會十子曰：「詩先成者賞。」

translations.literal: When Ai received an appointment, he gathered the Ten Talents and said: "Whoever finishes a poem first shall be rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: When Ai received an appointment, he gathered the Ten Talents and said: "Whoever finishes a poem first shall be rewarded."

sentences.zh: 時端先獻，警句云：「薰香荀令偏憐小，傅粉何郎不解愁。」

translations.literal: At the time Duan submitted first; his striking lines read: "The fragrant Lord Xun who loves the small, the powdered Lord He who knows not sorrow."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Duan submitted first; his striking lines read: "The fragrant Lord Xun who loves the small, the powdered Lord He who knows not sorrow."

sentences.zh: 主即以百縑賞之。

translations.literal: The princess immediately rewarded him with a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The princess immediately rewarded him with a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 錢起曰：「李校書誠有才，此篇宿構也。

translations.literal: Qian Qi said: "Secretary Li truly has talent, but this piece was composed beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Qi said: "Secretary Li truly has talent, but this piece was composed beforehand.

sentences.zh: 願賦一韻正之，請以起姓為韻。」

translations.literal: I wish to compose one rhyme in correction; please use my surname Qi as the rhyme."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to compose one rhyme in correction; please use my surname Qi as the rhyme."

sentences.zh: 端即襞箋而獻曰：「方塘似鏡草芊芊，初月如鉤未上弦。

translations.literal: Duan immediately folded paper and submitted: "A square pond like a mirror, grass lush and green; the new moon like a hook, not yet on the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: Duan immediately folded paper and submitted: "A square pond like a mirror, grass lush and green; the new moon like a hook, not yet on the bowstring.

sentences.zh: 新開金埒教調馬，舊賜銅山許鑄錢。」

translations.literal: The new golden paddock teaches horse training; the old grant of copper mountain permits coining money."
translations.idiomatic: The new golden paddock teaches horse training; the old grant of copper mountain permits coining money."

sentences.zh: 曖曰：「此愈工也。」

translations.literal: Ai said: "This is even more skillful."
translations.idiomatic: Ai said: "This is even more skillful."

sentences.zh: 起等始服。

translations.literal: Qi and the others at last submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and the others at last submitted.

sentences.zh: 端自校書郎移疾江南，授杭州司馬而卒。

translations.literal: Duan, from Secretary, took leave for illness in the Jiangnan region, was appointed Vice Director of Hang Prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Duan, from secretary, took leave for illness in the Jiangnan region, was appointed vice director of Hangzhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 虞仲亦工詩。

translations.literal: Yuzhong was also skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhong was also skilled in poetry.

sentences.zh: 元和初，登進士第，又以制策登科，授弘文校書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi examination, and also passed the policy examination; he was appointed Collator in the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe he passed the jinshi examination, and also passed the policy examination; he was appointed collator in the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 從事荊南，入為太常博士，遷兵部員外、司勛郎中。

translations.literal: He served in Jingnan, entered court as Doctor in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was transferred to Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of War and Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
